# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Santavy_2022_cefazolin"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics11111582> (open access)

Santavy et al. gave a single prophylactic 2 g intravenous bolus of cefazolin
30-60 min before cardiac surgery and sampled plasma richly through the
operation. The final Monolix model has two compartments with first-order
elimination. eGFR (CKD-EPI) acts on clearance, body surface area on the
central volume, and the type of bypass circuit on the peripheral volume.
Standard extracorporeal circulation (ECC) and minimally invasive
extracorporeal circulation (MiECC) are each compared with off-pump surgery.

# Population

Sixty-five adults were enrolled at University Hospital Olomouc, Czech Republic
(Results 2.1, Table 1). Twenty had off-pump surgery (17 male), 25 were operated
on MiECC (19 male) and 20 on standard ECC (19 male). Group medians were 68-73
years, 85-89 kg and a DuBois BSA of 1.98-2.01 m^2, with no significant
between-group differences. Median CKD-EPI eGFR was 1.36-1.52 mL/s/1.73 m^2
(about 82-91 mL/min/1.73 m^2); Results 2.3 gives the range of the whole study
as 0.67-2.8 mL/s. Surgery lasted a median 135 min off-pump, 198 min on ECC
and 191 min on MiECC. Bypass ran a median 124 min on ECC and 71 min on MiECC.
There were 461 plasma samples, taken at 15, 30, 45, 60, 120 and 180 min after
the dose and at the end of surgery.

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | `log(0.045 * 60)` = log(2.7 L/h) | Table 2, CL_pop = 0.045 (printed 'L/h', fitted per minute; see below) |
| `lvc` | `log(4.91)` L | Table 2, Vd1_pop |
| `lq` | `log(0.28 * 60)` = log(16.8 L/h) | Table 2, Q_pop = 0.28 (printed 'L/h', fitted per minute) |
| `lvp` | `log(22.07)` L | Table 2, Vd2_pop |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.49 per mL/s/1.73 m^2 | Table 2, beta_CL_eGFR |
| `e_bsa_vc` | 0.51 per m^2 | Table 2, beta_Vd1_BSA |
| `e_cpbstd_vp` | -0.77 | Table 2, beta_Vd2_ECC |
| `e_cpbmini_vp` | -0.79 | Table 2, beta_Vd2_MiECC |
| `etalcl` | 0.35^2 = 0.1225 | Table 2, omega_CL (SD) |
| `etalvc` | 0.10^2 = 0.01 | Table 2, omega_Vd1 (SD) |
| `etalq` | 0.77^2 = 0.5929 | Table 2, omega_Q (SD) |
| `etalvp` | 0.58^2 = 0.3364 | Table 2, omega_Vd2 (SD) |
| `propSd` | 0.16 | Table 2, 'Proportional' |
| `cl`, `vc`, `q`, `vp` covariate equations | log-linear, uncentered | Table 2 footnote |
| Two-compartment ODE, IV bolus into `central` | n/a | Results 2.2; Methods 3.3 |
| `crclSi <- CRCL / 60` | n/a | Table 1 reports eGFR in mL/s/1.73 m^2; the register column is mL/min/1.73 m^2 |

## The time unit of the clearances

Table 2 labels CL_pop and Q_pop in L/h, but the fit was in minutes: samples
were taken at 15-180 min, and the 407 min PTA horizon, the 215-318 min redosing
times and the time axes of Figures 1-4 are all in minutes. The chunk below
evaluates a typical patient both ways. Their eGFR is 1.42 mL/s, the cohort
median, with a BSA of 1.99 m^2 and surgery on MiECC. No random numbers are
involved.

```{r time-unit}
egfr <- 1.42
bsa <- 1.99
cl_raw <- 0.045 * exp(0.49 * egfr)
vc_t <- 4.91 * exp(0.51 * bsa)
vp_t <- 22.07 * exp(-0.79)
q_raw <- 0.28
c407 <- function(cl, q, t) {
  # Closed-form two-compartment IV bolus, 2000 mg.
  k10 <- cl / vc_t
  k12 <- q / vc_t
  k21 <- q / vp_t
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  a <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  b <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  2000 / vc_t * ((a - k21) / (a - b) * exp(-a * t) + (k21 - b) / (a - b) * exp(-b * t))
}
unit_check <- tibble::tibble(
  reading = c("per minute (used here)", "per hour (as printed)"),
  `CL (L/h)` = c(cl_raw * 60, cl_raw),
  `Cc at 407 min (mg/L)` = c(c407(cl_raw, q_raw, 407), c407(cl_raw / 60, q_raw / 60, 407))
)
knitr::kable(unit_check, digits = 2)
```

Read per minute, a typical patient clears 5.4 L/h, a usual cefazolin
clearance in cardiac surgery, and is at about 17 mg/L 407 min after the dose.
That is close to the 14-15 mg/L median of the middle panel of Figure 4, which
spans eGFR 1-2.17 mL/s and all three circuits. Read per
hour, clearance would be 0.09 L/h and the concentration would hardly fall
over the operation. That contradicts every panel of Figure 4 and the
redosing times the paper derives.

```{r time-unit-gate}
# Deterministic algebra, no RNG: a tight gate is appropriate. The x60
# conversion, a swapped beta or an additive reading of the covariate equations
# moves these by several-fold.
stopifnot(
  abs(unit_check$`CL (L/h)`[1] - 5.414) < 0.01,
  abs(unit_check$`Cc at 407 min (mg/L)`[1] - 17.25) < 0.05,
  unit_check$`Cc at 407 min (mg/L)`[2] > 100
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The simulations below use virtual patients
whose covariates follow Table 1. There are four arms of 200 patients each,
matching the populations of Table 3 and Figure 4:

* **Study population.** eGFR is log-normal with a median of 1.42 mL/s/1.73 m^2
  (the mean of the three group medians) and log-SD 0.28, truncated to the study
  range 0.67-2.8 mL/s.
* **eGFR 0.67-1, 1-2.17 and 2.17-2.8 mL/s.** These are the three panels of
  Figure 4. eGFR is uniform within each band. The last band is the "eGFR >= 2.17
  mL/s" (augmented renal clearance) column of Table 3.

In every arm BSA is normal with mean 1.99 m^2 and SD 0.17, truncated to
1.58-2.46 m^2. The circuit is drawn with the enrolled proportions: 20 off-pump,
25 MiECC and 20 ECC out of 65.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() seeds R's RNG (the covariate draw) only. rxode2's simulation RNG is
# partitioned per solver thread, so a CI runner with a different thread count
# draws different etas. Every assertion below is on a median or a proportion
# with a tolerance of at least 3 binomial standard errors, never on a tail value.
set.seed(20221109)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221109)

n_arm <- 200L
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, med, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  x <- numeric(0)
  while (length(x) < n) {
    y <- exp(rnorm(n, log(med), sdlog))
    x <- c(x, y[y >= lo & y <= hi])
  }
  x[seq_len(n)]
}
rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- numeric(0)
  while (length(x) < n) {
    y <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
    x <- c(x, y[y >= lo & y <= hi])
  }
  x[seq_len(n)]
}

make_cohort <- function(n, egfr, arm, id_offset) {
  circuit <- sample(c("off-pump", "MiECC", "ECC"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(20, 25, 20))
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    eGFR = egfr,
    CRCL = egfr * 60,
    BSA = rtrunc_norm(n, 1.99, 0.17, 1.58, 2.46),
    SURG_CPB_STD = as.integer(circuit == "ECC"),
    SURG_CPB_MINI = as.integer(circuit == "MiECC")
  )
}

arms <- c("Study population", "eGFR 0.67-1", "eGFR 1-2.17", "eGFR 2.17-2.8")
subj <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_arm, rtrunc_lnorm(n_arm, 1.42, 0.28, 0.67, 2.8), arms[1], 0L),
  make_cohort(n_arm, runif(n_arm, 0.67, 1), arms[2], 1L * n_arm),
  make_cohort(n_arm, runif(n_arm, 1, 2.17), arms[3], 2L * n_arm),
  make_cohort(n_arm, runif(n_arm, 2.17, 2.8), arms[4], 3L * n_arm)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subj$id))

# 2000 mg IV bolus at time 0 into the ODE state `central`. Observation rows also
# use cmt = "central"; Cc is returned as a column at those rows. Grid every
# 5 min to 405 min plus the 407 min PTA horizon, in hours (the model's unit).
t_obs_min <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 405, by = 5), 407)))
dose_rows <- subj |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 2000, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- subj |>
  tidyr::crossing(tmin = t_obs_min) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = tmin / 60, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::select(-tmin)
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dplyr::everything()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))

subj |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `eGFR median (mL/s)` = median(eGFR),
    `BSA median (m^2)` = median(BSA),
    `ECC (%)` = 100 * mean(SURG_CPB_STD),
    `MiECC (%)` = 100 * mean(SURG_CPB_MINI)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohort by arm.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Santavy_2022_cefazolin")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "eGFR")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tmin = round(time * 60))
# `Cc` is the individual prediction (no residual error); `sim` adds the
# proportional residual error.
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc)))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3: visual predictive check

```{r figure-3}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Santavy 2022: 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of
# simulated concentrations (with residual error) for the study population.
# The paper's VPC replicates its own 65 patients; this one uses the virtual
# study-population arm.
vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "Study population", tmin >= 15) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tmin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q10 = quantile(sim, 0.10),
    q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    q90 = quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(tmin)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q10), colour = "steelblue", linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q90), colour = "steelblue", linetype = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 180)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Cefazolin concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles, 2 g IV bolus",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Santavy 2022."
  )
```

The observed median in Figure 3 falls from about 105 mg/L at 15 min to about
55 mg/L at 60 min and about 33 mg/L at 180 min. The 90th percentile is about
140 mg/L at 15 min, and the 10th percentile about 20 mg/L at 200 min. These
values were read off the figure by the maintainers.

```{r figure-3-gate}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tmin, ~q50_fig,
  15, 105,
  60, 55,
  180, 33
)
fig3_cmp <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::left_join(vpc, by = "tmin") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (q50 / q50_fig - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(fig3_cmp) == 3, !anyNA(fig3_cmp$q50))
knitr::kable(fig3_cmp |> dplyr::select(tmin, q50_fig, q50, pct_diff), digits = 1)
# A median over 200 subjects is robust to which subjects land in the tails.
# A per-hour clearance (no decline), an additive covariate reading, or a
# Vd1/Vd2 swap moves these medians by far more than 25%.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct_diff) < 25))
```

```{r figure-4}

fig4 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm != "Study population", tmin >= 15) |>

  dplyr::summarise(

```

The Figure 4 medians at 407 min were read off the figure by the maintainers:
about 23, 14.5 and 7.5 mg/L for the three bands.

```{r figure-4-gate}
fig4_ref <- tibble::tibble(
  arm = factor(arms[2:4], levels = arms),
  p50_fig = c(23, 14.5, 7.5)
)
fig4_cmp <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::filter(tmin == 407) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, p50) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig4_ref, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (p50 / p50_fig - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(fig4_cmp) == 3)
knitr::kable(fig4_cmp, digits = 1)
# The three bands differ about three-fold at 407 min, so a wrong sign or unit
# on the eGFR effect fails here immediately; 30% leaves room for digitising
# error and for a 200-subject median.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff) < 30))
```

# Probability of target attainment (Table 3)

The paper's target is fT > MIC = 100% over the first 407 min. After a single
bolus the concentration only falls, so the target is met when the
concentration at 407 min exceeds the MIC. The PTA below uses individual
predictions without residual error. The "eGFR < 2.17" column is the
study-population arm restricted to eGFR < 2.17 mL/s.

```{r pta}
mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4)
c407_df <- sim |> dplyr::filter(tmin == 407)
pta_of <- function(x) vapply(mics, function(m) 100 * mean(x > m), numeric(1))
study407 <- c407_df$Cc[c407_df$arm == "Study population"]
study_egfr <- c407_df$eGFR[c407_df$arm == "Study population"]
arc407 <- c407_df$Cc[c407_df$arm == "eGFR 2.17-2.8"]
stopifnot(length(study407) == n_arm, length(arc407) == n_arm)
pta <- tibble::tibble(
  MIC = mics,
  sim_all = pta_of(study407),
  pub_all = c(99.7, 99.5, 98.8, 98.1, 97.2, 95.1, 92.6),
  sim_lt = pta_of(study407[study_egfr < 2.17]),
  pub_lt = c(99.8, 99.5, 99.0, 98.3, 97.4, 95.5, 93.1),
  sim_arc = pta_of(arc407),
  pub_arc = c(97.9, 96.1, 92.4, 88.7, 84.7, 77.1, 69.7)
)
pta |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC,
    "Study, simulated" = sim_all, "Study, Table 3" = pub_all,
    "eGFR < 2.17, simulated" = sim_lt, "eGFR < 2.17, Table 3" = pub_lt,
    "eGFR >= 2.17, simulated" = sim_arc, "eGFR >= 2.17, Table 3" = pub_arc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "PTA (%) for fT > MIC = 100% over 407 min.")

# Binomial SE with 200 subjects: about 1.9 points at a PTA of 92% and 3.2 points
# at 70%. The bounds are more than 3 SE wide and still fail when CL and Q are
# read per hour, which gives 100% at every MIC.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(pta$sim_all - pta$pub_all)) < 8,
  max(abs(pta$sim_arc - pta$pub_arc)) < 15,
  pta$sim_arc[pta$MIC == 4] < 90
)
```

## Redosing times for augmented renal clearance

Results 2.3 recommends a second dose in augmented renal clearance (eGFR >= 2.17
mL/s) at 215, 245, 288 and 318 min for MICs of 4, 3, 2 and 1.5 mg/L. Those are
the times when the 10th percentile of concentrations reaches the MIC. The
table gives the simulated crossing times with and without residual error. A
blank cell means the 10th percentile is still above the MIC at 407 min.

```{r redose}
arc_q10 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "eGFR 2.17-2.8", tmin >= 15) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tmin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q10_ipred = quantile(Cc, 0.10),
    q10_ruv = quantile(sim, 0.10),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cross_time <- function(mic, q10) {
  # Interpolate the first crossing of the MIC on the log scale.
  i <- which(q10 <= mic)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  t0 <- arc_q10$tmin[i - 1]
  t1 <- arc_q10$tmin[i]
  y0 <- log(q10[i - 1])
  y1 <- log(q10[i])
  t0 + (log(mic) - y0) / (y1 - y0) * (t1 - t0)
}
redose_mic <- c(4, 3, 2, 1.5)
redose <- tibble::tibble(
  `MIC (mg/L)` = redose_mic,
  `Results 2.3 (min)` = c(215, 245, 288, 318),
  `Simulated, no residual error (min)` = vapply(redose_mic, cross_time, numeric(1), q10 = arc_q10$q10_ipred),
  `Simulated, with residual error (min)` = vapply(redose_mic, cross_time, numeric(1), q10 = arc_q10$q10_ruv)
)
knitr::kable(redose, digits = 0)
# Known deviation, not gated against the published times (see below). The gate
# checks only that the 10th percentile of the augmented-renal-clearance arm
# reaches 4 mg/L inside the 407 min window, which Table 3 (PTA 69.7% at 4
# mg/L) requires and a per-hour clearance would not produce.
stopifnot(
  !is.na(redose$`Simulated, no residual error (min)`[1]),
  redose$`Simulated, no residual error (min)`[1] < 407
)
```

The simulated times are later than the published ones by about 1 to 1.5 h.
This is a known deviation, and the published times do not agree with the
paper's own Table 3. Table 3 gives a PTA of 88.7% at 1.5 mg/L over 407 min in
the same population, so about 11% of patients are below 1.5 mg/L at 407 min.
The 10th percentile therefore crosses 1.5 mg/L shortly before 407 min, not
at 318 min. In the same way, a PTA of 69.7% at 4 mg/L puts the 10th-percentile
crossing well before 407 min, but nothing in Table 3 supports one as early as
215 min. The model reproduces Table 3, as shown above. The paper does not say
how its redosing times were derived, and they are not used to judge the model.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental results. NCA on the simulated profiles
gives the exposure per eGFR band over the 407 min horizon. The terminal
half-life comes from the last part of that window and so describes the
operative period, not the full washout.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = 407 / 60,
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  clast.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "clast.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-407min (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
    "C at 407 min (mg/L)" = clast.obs,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA by arm.")
stopifnot(!anyNA(nca_summary$auclast))
# AUC must fall as eGFR rises; the 2.17-2.8 band has about 1.9-fold the
# clearance of the 0.67-1 band.
auc_lo <- nca_summary$auclast[nca_summary$arm == "eGFR 0.67-1"]
auc_hi <- nca_summary$auclast[nca_summary$arm == "eGFR 2.17-2.8"]
stopifnot(auc_lo / auc_hi > 1.2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Clearance time unit.** Table 2 prints CL_pop = 0.045 and Q_pop = 0.28 in
  L/h. The model was fitted with time in minutes, so the maintainers read both
  values per minute and multiplied them by 60 (2.7 and 16.8 L/h). The per-minute
  reading reproduces Table 3, Figure 4 and the redosing times above. The
  per-hour reading gives a clearance of 0.09 L/h and a PTA of 100% at every MIC.
- **Covariate equations.** The Table 2 footnote gives the Monolix log-linear
  form, `log(P) = log(P_pop) + beta * covariate`, with uncentered covariates.
  The model uses this form. The Abstract and Discussion read the coefficients
  additively ("increased by 0.49 L/h with each 1 mL/s/1.73 m^2", "a central Vd
  of 5.79 L in a patient with a BSA of 1.73 m^2", "reduction in Vd by only
  3.5%"). That reading is not used. Under the printed equation, the typical
  central volume at a BSA of 1.73 m^2 is 4.91 x exp(0.51 x 1.73) = 11.9 L, and
  either bypass circuit lowers the peripheral volume by about 54%, not 3.5%.
  The additive reading of the clearance gives 0.74 L/h (per hour) or 44 L/h
  (per minute) at the median eGFR. Neither is compatible with Figure 4.
- **eGFR units.** Table 1, Results 2.3 and the Discussion give eGFR in
  mL/s/1.73 m^2; the Abstract's "mL/min/1.73 m^2" is a misprint. The model's
  `CRCL` column is in mL/min/1.73 m^2 and is divided by 60 inside the model.
- **Table 1 misprint.** The ECC-group eGFR range is printed as "1.36
  (1.68-1.85)", which does not contain its own median. It is not used.
- **Bypass circuit covariates.** `SURG_CPB_STD` (standard ECC) and
  `SURG_CPB_MINI` (MiECC) are subject-level indicators of the circuit used for
  the operation. The maintainers registered them as new canonical columns. They
  are distinct from the time-varying intra-operative windows `CPB_ON` /
  `CPB_REWARM` / `CPB_POST`. The paper applies the effect to every observation
  of a patient, including those before bypass started.
- **Virtual cohort.** The paper gives eGFR only as group medians and ranges, so
  the study-population eGFR distribution (log-normal, median 1.42, log-SD 0.28,
  truncated to 0.67-2.8 mL/s) was chosen by the maintainers. Uniform
  distributions were used within the Figure 4 bands. BSA is normal around the
  Table 1 medians. Covariates were drawn independently.
- **Figure values.** The Figure 3 medians and Figure 4 medians at 407 min were
  read off the published figures by the maintainers and are approximate.
- **Redosing times not reproduced.** The 215-318 min redosing times of
  Results 2.3 come out 1 to 1.5 h later in the simulation. They are
  inconsistent with the paper's Table 3, which the model does reproduce, so
  they are shown but not used to judge the model.
- **PTA without residual error.** The simulated PTA uses individual predictions.
  The paper does not say whether its Simulx simulations included residual
  error.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Crossref or
  Europe PMC as of 2026-10-15.
